html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SLA: service level agreement

  • The Message Batches API: 50% cost savings, up to 24 hours, no latency guarantee, custom_id
  • Which workflows are batch-friendly and which are blocking
  • SLA arithmetic for submission windows, and how to resubmit failures
  • Self-review limits, independent instances, multi-pass reviews and confidence-based routing

2The Message Batches API (Task 4.5)

Running case

Birchwood Supply Wants a Smaller Bill

  • Two Claude workflows run in real time: (1) a live chat translator that customers wait on, and (2) a weekly refresh of 40,000 product descriptions that is published on Monday
  • The finance team says: "Move both to the batch API and save 50%"
Fact Detail
Saving 50% of the standard price
Time Results within up to 24 hours; many batches finish much sooner, but there is no guaranteed latency SLA
Matching (correlating) request and response pairs custom_id on each request (unique, 1 to 64 characters); results may come back in any order
Flow Create the batch → poll its status until it has ended → read results by custom_id
Tool calls A batch request is one model call: the API cannot run a tool mid-request and send the result back (no multi-turn tool calling inside a single request)

Workflow API
Live chat translation, pre-merge check (a person waits) Synchronous
Weekly product-description refresh, overnight technical-debt report Batch
Weekly audit of documents Batch
Nightly test generation Batch
Anything that needs an agentic tool loop Synchronous (loop in your code)
Exam tip

"50% cheaper" is not a reason to batch a blocking workflow. "Often finishes faster" is not an SLA.

[Verify live] Current documentation: most batches finish within an hour; results are available when all requests have finished or after 24 hours; a batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB; results stay downloadable for 29 days. A batch may include requests that define tools, but each request still ends after one response, so there is no tool-execution round trip. As of 8 November 2026.

Planning against an SLA

  • Worst case wait = time until the next submission + the 24-hour processing window.
  • Example: data must be processed within a 30-hour SLA. If you submit a batch every 4 hours, the worst case is 4 + 24 = 28 hours, which meets the SLA with margin. Submitting once a day (24 + 24 = 48 hours) does not.

Handling failures and improving first-pass success

  • Some requests in a batch may fail (for example a document too long for the context window). Resubmit only the failed ones, found by custom_id, with changes such as chunking the oversized document.
  • Refine the prompt on a small sample first before submitting thousands of documents, to maximize first-pass success and reduce the cost of iterative resubmission.
Exam tip

A blocking step (someone waits) is never a batch job; compute the interval as interval + 24 hours ≤ SLA.

3Multi-Instance and Multi-Pass Review (Task 4.6)

Why self-review is weak

  • A model that just produced code retains its reasoning context, so in the same session it is less likely to question its own decisions.
  • An independent review instance (no prior reasoning context) is more effective at catching subtle issues than telling the same session to "review carefully" or turning on extended thinking.

Multi-pass review

Pass Purpose
Per-file local passes Consistent depth on each file; avoids attention dilution
Cross-file integration pass Cross-file data flow and interface issues
Verification pass The model self-reports a confidence for each finding, enabling calibrated routing (low-confidence findings to human review)
Exam tip

"Run it three times and keep only findings that appear twice" hides real bugs that a single run catches only sometimes. Prefer independent, differently scoped passes.

4Exam Q&A

S1The company proposes moving both the live chat translator and the weekly description refresh to the Message Batches API for the 50% saving. What is the best evaluation?

  • ABatch both and poll for completion
  • BBatch both and fall back to real time if a batch is slow
  • CKeep both synchronous
  • DBatch the weekly refresh; keep the live translator on the synchronous API
Show the answer

Answer: D. Batches may take up to 24 hours with no guaranteed latency, which suits the weekly refresh but not a customer who is waiting. The fallback design adds complexity that matching each workflow to the right API avoids.

S2What identifies which batch result belongs to which request?

  • AThe title of the document that each request was built from
  • BThe order in which the results come back from the API
  • CThe timestamp
  • DThe custom_id set on each request
Show the answer

Answer: D. Results can arrive in any order, so correlate with custom_id.

S3Records must be processed within a 30-hour SLA, and a batch takes up to 24 hours. What submission interval is safe?

  • AEvery 12 hours, which leaves enough margin for the 24-hour processing time
  • BWhenever convenient for the team, as long as batches are eventually sent
  • COnce a day
  • DEvery 4 hours (worst case 28 hours)
Show the answer

Answer: D. Worst-case wait is the interval plus 24 hours; 4 + 24 = 28 fits inside 30. The other intervals break the SLA.

S4In a batch of 500 supplier contracts, eight fail because they exceed the context limit. What is the best response?

  • AResubmit the whole batch
  • BDrop them silently
  • CResubmit only the eight failed documents (by custom_id), chunked
  • DSwitch all documents to the synchronous API and drop the batch entirely
Show the answer

Answer: C. Resubmit failures only, with a modification that addresses the cause.

S5Before running 20,000 documents through a batch, what should the team do to reduce rework?

  • AIncrease the batch size
  • BSubmit everything and fix problems afterwards
  • CUse the largest possible prompt
  • DRefine the prompt on a representative sample first
Show the answer

Answer: D. Prompt refinement on a sample maximizes first-pass success and avoids expensive iterative resubmission.

S6Why can a batch request not drive a full agentic tool loop?

  • ATools are always disabled
  • BBatches are too small
  • CBatch requests only support plain text, so tool definitions are rejected outright
  • DA request is a single model call, so tools cannot be executed mid-request and their results sent back
Show the answer

Answer: D. A tool round trip needs another request; a batch request ends after one response.

S7The same session that wrote a function reviews it and reports "no issues", yet a colleague finds a subtle bug. What is the best architecture?

  • ASwitch off reviews
  • BReview only the formatting
  • CAsk the same session to think harder and turn on extended thinking for the review
  • DUse an independent Claude instance that lacks the generator's reasoning
Show the answer

Answer: D. The generator's reasoning context makes self-review less critical; an independent instance catches more.

S8A team wants to send only uncertain review findings to a human. Which design supports that?

  • ARandomly sampling findings
  • BSending everything to humans so that no finding is ever missed or ignored
  • CA verification pass in which the model reports a confidence per finding
  • DSending nothing to humans
Show the answer

Answer: C. Per-finding confidence enables routing of limited human attention (with calibration, covered in Module 14).

S9Which TWO workloads suit the Message Batches API? Select TWO.

  • AA live customer chat
  • BAn approval step a person is waiting on
  • CAn overnight technical-debt report
  • DA pre-merge check that blocks developers
  • EA weekly audit of supplier contracts
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Batches suit latency-tolerant, non-blocking jobs. Anything a person or process waits on needs the synchronous API.

S10Which TWO practices strengthen a multi-pass review design? Select TWO.

  • APer-file local passes plus a cross-file integration pass
  • BUsing an independent review instance
  • CKeeping only findings reported in at least two of three runs
  • DOne single pass over every changed file
  • EAsking the same session to review its own work with extended thinking
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Focused passes and an independent instance counter attention dilution and self-review bias. Consensus filtering hides real findings.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Batches API 50% cheaper · up to 24 h · no latency SLA · custom_id · poll for completion
Good for Overnight reports, weekly audits, nightly test generation
Bad for Blocking work (pre-merge checks) and agentic tool loops
SLA math Interval + 24 h ≤ SLA (4 h + 24 h = 28 h ≤ 30 h)
Failures Resubmit only failed custom_ids, chunk oversized docs
Before volume Tune the prompt on a sample
Self-review Weak: generator keeps its reasoning
Better Independent instance · per-file passes + integration pass · verification pass with confidence for routing
